evidence: Cic. Fam. 13.20.1: meamque commendātiōnem ūsuī magnō sibi fuisse
Cic. Fam. 7.18.1: ego enim renovābō commendātiōnem
terms.comment: The thirteenth book of Cicero’s letters to his friends is almost all references of this kind.

evidence: Cic. Fam. 13.20.1: hunc igitur tibi commendō

terms.grammar: litterae, litterārum f. pl., with the adjective commendātīcius, -a, -um
evidence: Cic. Fam. 5.5.1: nūllās ad tē litterās mittere nisi commendātīciās

phrases.latin: hunc igitur tibi commendō et ā tē petō ut dēs operam ut intellegat dīligenter mē scrīpsisse dē sēsē meamque commendātiōnem ūsuī magnō sibi fuisse
phrases.english: So I recommend him to you, and ask you to see to it that he understands I wrote about him with care and that my reference did him a great deal of good

phrases.latin: etsī statueram nūllās ad tē litterās mittere nisi commendātīciās
phrases.english: although I had decided to send you no letters but letters of recommendation

commendaticius.html: Adjectives in -īcius made from perfect participles have a long ī, and Lewis & Short marks it so in ēmptīcius, conductīcius, missīcius, trālātīcius, adventīcius; only its commendātĭcĭus and collātĭcĭus stand apart.
